3 · Authorship, contributors and maximum byline size

Authorship is contribution- and accountability-based. The journal uses a standard operational maximum of 12 individually named authors for ordinary bylines. Manuscripts with more than 12 genuine qualifying authors require editor approval and should use group/collaborative authorship or an approved continuation sheet. This cap is an editorial workflow rule, not a reason to remove a contributor who ethically qualifies for authorship.

To qualify as an author, an individual must have made a substantial scholarly contribution; participated in drafting or critical intellectual review; approved the final version; and agreed to be accountable for the integrity of the work. Contributors who do not meet the full authorship threshold should be acknowledged rather than added as honorary, guest or gift authors.
Exactly one corresponding author must be designated for journal communication.
Author order must be agreed by the group before submission.
Every multi-author article must include a CRediT contribution statement using the 14-role taxonomy where appropriate.

Changes to authorship after submission require a reason and written agreement from all affected authors; disputes are referred to the relevant institution rather than adjudicated by the journal on contribution facts.
AI tools cannot be listed as authors.
No author names, affiliations, acknowledgements or identifying metadata.
Author order, ORCID, affiliations, corresponding author, declarations and keywords.
Editable or high-resolution source files as applicable, with permissions and captions.
Completed after acceptance and before final publication.

Specific, informative, searchable; avoid unsupported causal language.
4–8 precise indexing terms; avoid simply repeating the title.
Design, setting, data/materials, procedure, measures, analysis, reproducibility and ethics appropriate to the work.
Report evidence without interpretation inflation; include uncertainty where relevant.
Principal meaning, comparison with prior work, alternatives, limitations and implications.
Answer the study aim proportionately; do not introduce new evidence.
Ethics/consent, funding, conflicts, contributions, data/code, AI disclosure and permissions as applicable.
Consistent scholarly style, reconciled with in-text citations, DOI/URL checked where available.

Primary data, secondary data, simulation, benchmark results, experiments, expert judgement and inference must be clearly distinguished. Authors should describe enough detail for a competent reader to understand how evidence was generated and analysed.
Name the design; state place and relevant dates/period.
Eligibility, source, sampling or provenance, sample-size basis and exclusions.
Replicable sequence, intervention/exposure, equipment/software configuration and quality controls.
Definitions, units, validity/reliability or calibration, coding and missing-data handling.
Statistical, qualitative, computational or engineering method; assumptions; uncertainty; baselines/comparators; sensitivity checks.
Approving body/reference, consent, privacy, animal/community/safety protections, or justified not-applicable/exemption statement.
Number tables and figures in order of first citation; cite each in the text.
Use editable tables with real header rows. Do not submit screenshots of tables.
Figures must remain legible at publication size and include descriptive captions and alt text.
Use colour as a supplement, not the sole carrier of meaning; maintain readable contrast.
Equations must remain editable and variables defined on first use.
Obtain permission for third-party material and clearly identify material excluded from the article’s open licence.

Reference metadata should be checked against authoritative records where possible. A DOI match does not establish that a source supports a claim; authors and editors must evaluate the cited source itself. Retractions, corrections and version status should be checked for materially important citations.
The journal inserts only formally assigned ISSN and DOI information. “Pending” remains the correct publication-control state until registration is complete.

Generative AI may assist drafting, coding, analysis or editing only under accountable human oversight. It cannot be credited as an author, cannot be used to fabricate evidence or citations, and must not receive confidential or personal data without authority and appropriate safeguards.

CHIATECH JOURNAL follows an author-retained copyright model for open-access scholarly articles. Authors grant the publisher the right of first publication and the non-exclusive rights necessary to produce, distribute, preserve, index, deposit metadata and maintain the version of record. Unless an article records another approved licence, published scholarly content is released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).
Authors retain copyright unless an employer or other legal rights holder owns the work.
CC BY 4.0 permits sharing and adaptation, including commercial reuse, provided appropriate attribution is given and changes are indicated.
The journal does not add restrictions that contradict the applicable Creative Commons licence.
Third-party content not covered by the article licence must be clearly credited and permission-safe.
Authors remain responsible for obtaining permissions for copyrighted images, tables, instruments or substantial excerpts.
11 · Peer review, revision and proof approval

Automated readiness checks support editorial triage but do not decide acceptance. The journal uses qualified human editorial review and independent double-blind peer review where applicable. After acceptance, the corresponding author coordinates all co-author corrections and approves the final version of record only after checking content, author metadata, figures/tables, declarations, DOI/ISSN status, licence and accessibility.

Submission and peer review are free. Payment, ability to pay or a waiver request must not influence reviewer selection, peer-review reports or acceptance. Standard accepted-article APC: ₦35,000. Pioneer APC: ₦25,000 for Volumes 1 and 2 (July/August 2026), payable only after written acceptance and an official invoice. Authors should use only verified publisher payment instructions.
